minutes.headline: Water commissioners heard a clean FY21-22 audit, told the Howard Street developer no, and voted to only acknowledge the Woodlands letter.
minutes.summary: The CPA reviewed the FY21-22 audit and reported the district in a good financial position. A developer pressed the board about water service for his Howard Street project and was told the board would wait on the ZBA and a district vote. The board also debated sending the Woodlands road letter to counsel, settled on a bare acknowledgment, and heard superintendent updates on the Mass Ave project, a new well, tank inspection and lead service line funding.

public_comment.topic: Developer of the Howard Street project asked whether the district would let him run a main and meter pit at the district line and sell water to himself via a water company; discussed ZBA/HAC authority and attorney letters.

votes.motion: File the Woodlands letter (then softened to having Fran send an acknowledgment only)

budget_items.what_was_said: Sales were down from the prior year, which the CPA attributed to pandemic-era higher home water use fading.
Other revenue such as service connections rose, consistent with more building.
figures_as_heard: a hundred and nineteen thousand dollars

budget_items.what_was_said: Depreciation rose because the new district building was capitalized and is now depreciated.
Group insurance fell partly because some of the expense lands in the OPEB line.
Supplies fell as a new repairs and maintenance line absorbed some items.
Total operating expenses rose modestly and income from operations dropped.
Rental income declined but a tenant (T-Mobile) renewed and rent is expected to return toward earlier levels.
Interest expense rose with new bonds, driving the decrease in net position, which the CPA expects to partly reverse.
Cash rose and receivables and accounts payable shifted; short-term notes were refinanced to long term.
Upcoming annual debt and interest payments were read out and decline over the next years.
Both retiree health and pension liabilities declined.
figures_as_heard: a hundred and thirteen thousand dollars

budget_items.what_was_said: New budget numbers were requested because the original estimate from three years ago is outdated; an increase may need annual or special meeting action.
Members worried more attorney spending could force higher water prices.
A warrant article must appropriate money first and principal forgiveness would return it later; deadline for DEP submittal was stated.
A separate appropriation for GIS may be needed if the program does not cover it.

decisions.decision: Board's stance to the developer: it would not enter agreements on outside-district service without another district vote and will await the ZBA/HAC outcome.
Fran to send a simple acknowledgment of receipt of the Woodlands attorney letter; no referral to district counsel for now.
Woodlands matter to go at the bottom of a future agenda as unresolved discussion.
H2 Properties (110 Bird Street area) deferred to the next meeting in February.
Lead service line proposals to be brought back in about two weeks, with warrant articles drafted by end of February.
FY23-24 budget finalization held to the end, in executive session.

what_happened.line: The board gave the Howard Street developer no commitment on water service outside the district, saying it would await the ZBA outcome and another district vote.
The board agreed only to have Fran send an acknowledgment of receipt of the Woodlands attorney letter, with no referral to district counsel for now.
The CPA's review of the FY21-22 audit reported the district in a good financial position, with interest on new bonds the main driver of a lower net position.
The H2 Properties water main extension was postponed to the February meeting, and finalizing the FY23-24 budget was held to the end, in executive session.
Lead service line proposals are to return in about two weeks, with warrant articles drafted by the end of February.

why_it_matters: Whether the district sells water outside its boundaries, as the Howard Street developer asked, would need another district vote, so residents who vote at district meetings may be asked to decide it.

Lead service line funding and possible warrant articles, along with a Mass Ave project estimate now out of date, could bring spending and borrowing questions to a district meeting that affect water rates.
watch_next: The February meeting, where H2 Properties is scheduled and the FY23-24 budget is to be finalized.
Lead service line proposals due back in about two weeks, with warrant articles drafted by the end of February.
